app: GitHub Enterprise Server: in the Management Console go to Authentication and select SAML. GitHub Enterprise Cloud: on github.com go to your enterprise > Settings > Authentication security and enable SAML SSO (check your app's current UI).
Set the Sign-on URL to {idp_sso_url} and the Issuer to {idp_entity_id}, then paste the public certificate from {idp_cert_url}.
Choose signature method RSA-SHA256 and digest method SHA-256 when asked.

GitHub's own values: the entity ID is https://{host} and the consumer URL is https://{host}/saml/consume. For Enterprise Cloud on github.com use https://github.com/enterprises/{enterprise} and https://github.com/enterprises/{enterprise}/saml/consume (check your app's current UI).
Save and test authentication - on Enterprise Cloud keep 'Require SAML SSO authentication' off until the test passes.
flareid: Add a SAML service provider (Admin > Applications > SAML service providers > New) and apply this template.
Replace {host} with the GHES hostname, or with github.com/enterprises/{enterprise} for Enterprise Cloud - entity ID and ACS URL must both change.

The template uses a persistent NameID (the user's stable external id) and sends username/full_name/emails attributes, which is the attribute vocabulary GitHub Enterprise Server reads (check your app's current UI).
If your GitHub matches on email instead, switch NameID format to emailAddress.
